title: Read the Role Profile Catalog
subtitle: The governed matrix of what each role gets
scenario: It is SD-5. Before you plan any provisioning, read the reference People Ops owns: the role profile catalog. It says exactly what a Logistics Coordinator gets on day one - accounts, software, hardware, access groups, and pay class. Understand who owns it and why access is granted by role, not by request.
input: Role Profile: Logistics Coordinator (Operations). Accounts: identity, email, directory. Software: Logistics Suite, Email/Calendar. Hardware: Standard laptop. Access groups: ops-general, warehouse-readonly. Pay class: Non-exempt / Hourly. Owned by the People Ops Lead; entitlement changes require People Ops sign-off.
instructions: Read the role profile as the governed source for what this role gets.
Answer the four questions about ownership, least-privilege, and reuse.
Validate to mint the role profile record.

questions.prompt: Who owns the role profile catalog?

options.text: The IT Provisioner, who edits it per hire
The People Ops Lead, who governs entitlement changes
The hiring manager for each new hire

questions.explain: The People Ops Lead owns the catalog and governs changes. Provisioners read it; they do not edit what a role gets per hire.

questions.prompt: How is the new hire's access decided?

options.text: By the access groups the role profile lists - access by role
By whatever the new hire requests on day one
By copying the last hire in the department

questions.explain: Access is granted by role, not by request or by copying a colleague. The profile's groups (ops-general, warehouse-readonly) are the least-privilege default.

questions.prompt: Why does the catalog list a pay class per role?

options.text: So the hardware team knows which laptop to order
So the payroll handoff enrolls the hire in the right class without guessing
It is only for display and has no downstream use

questions.explain: The pay class (Non-exempt / Hourly) flows to the payroll task so enrollment is correct by role, not decided ad hoc.

questions.prompt: Which later step expands this profile into concrete tasks?
questions.explain: The Provisioning Plan expands the role profile into one owned, dated task per entitlement. The gate only reads the results later.

copilotPrompt: Explain a role profile catalog for onboarding: who owns it, why access is granted by role rather than by request (least-privilege), why a pay class lives per role, and which step expands it into tasks.
successMessage: Role profile read. You now hold the governed matrix the provisioning plan expands.

intro.heading: Before you plan: what the role gets

sections.title: A catalog, not a guess
sections.body: What a Logistics Coordinator gets on day one is not decided per hire. It lives in a governed catalog People Ops owns, so every hire in the role gets the same, auditable set.

sections.title: Access by role is least-privilege
sections.body: Granting exactly the access groups the profile lists - and nothing more - is how least-privilege is enforced. A grant the profile does not list is a policy exception, not a convenience.

sections.title: One profile, many readers
sections.body: The provisioning plan, the access task, and the payroll handoff all read this profile. Getting the catalog right once is what keeps four parallel branches consistent.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: Reading the profile mints a role profile record the plan expands. Later, the archive loop feeds real usage back so the catalog keeps improving.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd keep a table of role to entitlements and read the row for this role, rather than deciding per hire what accounts and access to grant.

bestFit.how: a Dataverse entitlements table with an owner in People Ops, edited through a form
a database read keyed on role, returning the entitlement list the plan expands

takeaway.heading: Role profile read
points: You confirmed the People Ops Lead owns the catalog and governs entitlement changes.
Access is granted by role (ops-general, warehouse-readonly) - least-privilege by default.
The pay class flows to payroll so enrollment is correct by role, not by guess.
Your role profile record is stored for the provisioning plan to expand.
The workflow can now say exactly what this role gets on day one.
